questions.q: Bertrand's Box Paradox: a cabinet has three drawers. One holds two gold coins, one holds two silver coins, and one holds one gold and one silver coin. A class takes a test. The students who scored in the top 10% are given a harder retest the next day, and on average they score lower the second time. A teacher concludes the harder test caused the drop. Is that conclusion justified?
choices: Yes, but only because the grading got stricter overnight
Yes — the second test was objectively harder, so it must have caused the lower scores
No — this is regression to the mean: unusually high scores tend to be followed by scores closer to average even without any real change
No, because test scores are entirely random and carry no information
